headline: Wastewater deputy commissioner updates $28 million CSO 4583 sewer project and recent street paving.
summary: Polita was awarded the work this summer and has finished about three or four percent, the wastewater deputy commissioner said. The work will take a couple of years, with most of it coming in the next construction season. A new outfall near the GE building may be built over the winter. Separately, paving on the CSO 32 streets is complete except for some remaining items, and a second phase is set for next year.
discussion: CSO 4583 sewer project: Crews are picking at areas on Central Street and Davis Street before winter. The deputy commissioner said the project is three or four percent complete.
CSO 32 street paving: Streets were paved curb to curb rather than with trench patches, to limit damage from trucks and equipment. Some remaining items, including gate boxes, will be repaved.

Utility of the Year award: The New England Water Works Association named the division 2026 Utility of the Year. A representative cited work including a $11.6 million investment in downtown water main replacement.
Montachusett Industrial Park pump station: Four bids were received. Staff plans to go with the low bid from Duschene Construction Group, and the contract is being prepared for signature.
